cards.text: Jesus has been in Bethany, where they hosted a dinner for Him. The next day, the great crowd in town for the feast hears that Jesus is coming to Jerusalem. Friend, that news moves faster than a group chat after somebody texts “Big news. Call me.”

cards.question: The crowd grabs ___ branches and goes out to meet Jesus.

cards.text: Out they go, and they are LOUD. “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

cards.question: The crowd going out to meet Jesus also shouts that He is the King of Israel.

cards.text: Now Jesus, on His way to Jerusalem, finds something and sits on it. Me, I'd hop in on my gold base and get there NEXT Tuesday.

cards.question: Jesus finds a young ___ and sits on it.
John says Jesus sat on that young donkey just as something said He would. What?
Those written words speak to the Daughter of Zion about her King coming on a donkey's colt. What do they tell her?
The disciples are right there for all of this. True or false: they understand what it means right away.

cards.text: Not at first, friend. It clicks for them later, the way a joke finally hits me three days after somebody told it, and I'm laughing alone in the bakery at nothing.

cards.question: The disciples remember what was done to Jesus and realize it was written about Him after He was ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, there are many people who were with Jesus the day He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.

cards.question: What do the people who saw Jesus raise Lazarus keep doing?
John gives another reason the crowd went out to meet Jesus. What is it?

answers.text: They heard He would be crowned
They heard He was giving gifts

cards.text: Then the Pharisees, a group of Jewish religious leaders, huddle up and talk it over with one another.

cards.question: Watching the crowd, the Pharisees tell one another that what they are doing against Jesus is working.

cards.text: Not even close: “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!” Friend, that's me at the bakery door yelling “Ovens aren't READY!” while every baker walks right past me.

findings.problem: The question types follow a repeating pattern. After the first two choice cards, the sequence fill in the blank, multiple choice, multiple choice, true or false (cards 6, 7, 8, 9) repeats exactly (cards 11, 13, 14, 16).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. "Hop in on my gold base" makes the base sound like a car. The punchline is about travel speed, but the moment is about Jesus finding something to sit on. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Lazarus shows up here for the first time in the lesson, and the card never says who he is. For example, it could call him Jesus' friend from Bethany (John 11:1-3), with the reference.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card tells of a man raised from the dead with flat narration. It has no reaction, disbelief or anything else in Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says "what they are doing against Jesus." The passage only says "this is doing you no good" (John 12:19) and never says what "this" refers to. The card fills in something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. The Pharisees talk among themselves about their failure while the world goes after Jesus. In the joke, Papa Dorin is yelling at bakers to stop them as they walk past, which is a different action. "Ovens aren't READY!" also goes against his mission, because his job is to keep the ovens ready.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
